title: Shave a care manikin's left cheek and jaw with an electric shaver, the other hand holding the cheek skin taut
instruction: Shave the beard on the manikin's left cheek and jaw with the electric shaver without pressing hard or touching its lips, nose, eye or ear, then put the shaver back on its tray.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00, 1.5 million US jobs, BLS 2025: "Wash, groom, shave, or drape patients") and home health aides (31-1121.00: help with "dressing and grooming"; 4.7 million with personal care aides) shave residents. The nurse-aide checklist (Reuter, Nursing Assistant, CC BY): "Hold the shaver at a right angle to the resident's face, using your free hand to pull their skin taught as you shave. This will minimize snagging and the risk of cutting the resident." Philips's S3000 manual: "Stretch your skin with your free hand so the blades can lift and cut hair"; "Do not press too hard as too much pressure can cause shaving heads to pinch the skin." One hand holds the soft cheek skin pulled up toward the temple (it springs back when let go) while the other keeps a rotary shaver flat on the curved cheek and jaw with a light press, clear of the lips, nose, eye and ear.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. A life-size adult male care-training head and neck (rigid vinyl, 2.0 kg; 15.2 cm wide, 23.6 cm chin to crown, jaw 11.6 cm wide at its angles, ears 6.1 cm long) stands seated upright on a weighted base (14 cm across, fixed), on a sprung neck (1 N pushed into the cheek moves it about 0.8 mm), its face toward the robot's left (+y) and its left side toward the robot; the midpoint of its ear canals is at x 30, y 0, 19 cm up. The stubble-shaded beard area on its left cheek and jaw (38 cm2) spans x 22.9 to 27.9, y 1.8 to 8.3, 9.8 to 18.1 cm up. A soft skin insert over the left cheekbone (3.0 x 2.2 cm, centred at x 22.7, y 4.0, 21.1 cm up) slides up toward the temple 0 to 8 mm on a 0.12 N/mm spring. A three-head rotary electric shaver (16.1 x 5.8 x 4.5 cm, 170 g; heads 2 cm across; its head unit pivots up to 20 degrees and presses in up to 6 mm on a 1 N/mm spring) lies on its back, heads toward the head (+x), in a white tray (20 x 9 cm, 1 cm walls, fixed) centred at x 14, y 20. The head is held by its sprung neck; the shaver is loose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step from the head's, the skin insert's, the shaver's and its head unit's poses and the grippers' joints. The beard area (the stubble-shaded skin on the left side: 1.8 cm in front of the ear canals to 2 cm left of the chin's midline, from the cheek line down to where the skin under the jaw faces the table at 30 degrees, at least 2.4 cm from the lips, 2.2 cm from the nostril and 1.6 cm from the eye and ear; 38 cm2) is sampled at 593 points about 3 mm apart. A point is shaved when one of the three heads passes over it: inside the head's 20 mm circle and within 1.5 mm of its face, the head unit within 20 degrees of flat to the skin there, while the head unit's spring reads 0.3 to 3 N (1 N per mm pressed in, less its own weight). On the soft cheek (the 372 points behind a line 7.2 cm in front of the ear canals and above one 6.2 cm below them) it counts only while the skin insert is pulled 3 mm or more toward the temple: unstretched, the skin bunches and its hairs lie flat. 0 for the rest of the run if: the spring reads over 5 N (pressing hard enough to pinch the skin); a head comes within 1 mm of the lips, the left nostril, the left eye or the left ear; a gripper's finger touches the left eye; the head is pushed 8 mm from where it stood (at the middle of the beard area); or the shaver falls 3 cm or more with no gripper holding it. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 when at least 95% is shaved and the shaver rests on its tray (lowest point within 4 mm of the tray floor, its middle over the tray), let go (both gripper centres 5 cm or more from it) and still (within 1.5 mm) for 1 s; 0.75 when at least 95% is shaved but the shaver is not back; 0.5 at least 70%; 0.25 at least 30%; 0 otherwise, also when nothing is done. Real trial (parts, drawings and calibration in fabrication/): the rebuilt shaver's head unit sits on a 1 N/mm spring over a 5 N force sensor and the shaver logs its force every 50 ms; washable UV training gel (not powder) on the beard area only, lit by a UV torch, goes dark where a head wipes it; a side video gives each 3 mm square's last glowing and first dark frame, and the square counts when over that time the log reaches 0.3 N and stays at or under 3 N (on the soft cheek with the insert's dot 3 mm or more up on a mm scale whenever the log reads 0.3 N or more); a UV photo with a 3 mm grid card gives the count. 0 if the log reads 5 N; lipstick or eyeliner from the lips, nostril, eye or ear is found on a head, or eyeliner from the eyelids on a gripper's finger cot; a pin at the beard middle's height moves 7 mm over a mm card (the head pushed 8 mm); or the video shows a drop.
reset_notes: Wash the gel off the face and the shaver's heads, rub a thin even layer of gel on the beard area only again, redraw the lipstick on the lips and eyeliner on the nostril rims, eyelids and ear, change the gripper's finger cots if marked; check that the skin insert springs back to 0 and the head stands upright; lay the shaver on its back in its tray, heads toward the head; tap its head unit once with the log and video running. In simulation each trial starts afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz control. Hair, the tracer gel and the skin's give are not simulated: a point is shaved by the cutting rule; the soft cheek is a rigid 30 x 22 mm insert on a sprung slide, the rest of the face rigid. The head is built from its measurements, not a scan (colliders within 1.2 mm of its skin over the beard). The three heads float as one unit (+-20 deg, 6 mm on 1 N/mm), not singly. The real force-sensing shaver is 1.5 cm longer, its cutters still.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (it held both grippers back for most of the run, then lowered the left one over the shaver in its tray without taking it and moved the right one to the back of the neck; nothing was shaved); demo: 1.0
